 AFP Adhe Makayasa 20 Oct 2026 09:00-04:00 Arsenal vs Bayern Munich: Classic match - late London drama as Arsenal stun the German giants at the Emirates
 Arsenal Arsenal vs Bayern Munich Bayern Munich Champions League Premier League Bundesliga Classic match Relive the electrifying night in October 2015 when Arsenal defied the odds to defeat Pep Guardiola's Bayern Munich. Late goals from Olivier Giroud and Mesut Ozil secured a famous 2-0 victory in north London.
 There is a specific kind of electricity that crackles through the North London air on Champions League nights, particularly when the Bavarian behemoths of Bayern roll into town. In October 2015, the Emirates Stadium bore witness to a tactical chess match that eventually exploded into a night of pure, unadulterated Arsenal folklore. It was a time when Pep's Bayern were considered an immovable object, yet Arsene Wenger's men found a way to strike with the precision of a master thief in the night. 
 The tactical stalemate in North London
 For much of the encounter, the two sides engaged in a high-stakes stand-off. Bayern dominated possession with their trademark fluidity, forcing Petr Cech into several world-class interventions to keep the Gunners level. At the other end, Manuel Neuer proved why he was the gold standard for goalkeepers, producing a truly astonishing point-blank save from a Theo Walcott header that left the home support clutching their heads in disbelief. The tension was thick, the margin for error non-existent, and as the clock ticked into the final quarter, a goalless draw seemed the most likely outcome. 
 AFP Giroud breaks the Bavarian resistance
 The breakthrough finally arrived in the 77th minute, born from a moment of uncharacteristic hesitation in Bayern's backline. A looping free-kick was sent into the heart of the penalty area, and for once, the impenetrable Neuer misjudged the flight of the ball. The ever-alert Giroud, introduced as a second-half substitute to provide a physical focal point, capitalised on the goalkeeper's rare error. The Frenchman made contact to bundle the ball into the net, sending the Emirates into a state of absolute delirium as the German wall finally crumbled. 
 The tension of the final minutes
 Bayern, stung by the opener, poured forward in search of an equaliser, leaving themselves vulnerable to the counter-attack. The atmosphere was a cauldron of anxiety and hope as the fourth official signalled three minutes of added time. Arsenal remained disciplined, retreating into a compact shape and waiting for one final opportunity to kill the game. The fans were on their feet, whistling for the final whistle, sensing that one of their most significant European results of the modern era was within their grasp.

 Deep into stoppage time, the knockout blow was delivered. Hector Bellerin, showing incredible energy so late in the game, intercepted a loose pass and surged down the right flank. His low, fizzing cross found Ozil, whose shot was desperately clawed back by Neuer. In the pre-goal-line technology era, the Emirates held its breath as the official behind the goal made a decisive and correct call, signalling that the ball had crossed the line. The 2-0 scoreline was confirmed, and the victory was complete. 
 A night to remember at the Emirates
 This match remains a cherished memory for the Arsenal faithful, a rare moment of triumph against a Bayern side that had often proved their nemesis. It wasn't just about the three points in the group stage; it was about the resilience and clinical nature of a performance that subdued one of Europe's greatest teams. Under the floodlights, Wenger's Arsenal proved they could still mix it with the very best, leaving the German giants humbled and the North London night echoing with songs of victory.
